Examples of creditable experience include: Knowledge of IC policies, entities, missions, resources, operations, capabilities, and requirements to perform intelligence research, determine potential sources of information, and understand potential originators of information; and knowledge of National Disclosure Policy (NDP-1) and its application in the review and approval of intelligence and non-intelligence information for release to foreign governments combined with an understanding of how such policies fit within broader US foreign policy and national security objectives. Note: Creditable experience may include previous military experience, experience gained in the private sector, or experience gained in another government agency. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of IC policies, entities, missions, resources, operations, capabilities, and requirements to perform intelligence research, determine potential sources of information, and understand potential originators of information. Knowledge of National Disclosure Policy (NDP-1) and its application in the review and approval of intelligence and non-intelligence information for release to foreign governments combined with an understanding of how such policies fit within broader US foreign policy and national security objectives. Skill in conducting unbiased, difficult research, identify appropriate systems/data sources, and identifying the appropriate policy that would apply to such information for the purpose of determining appropriateness of sharing and who is the proper authority to approve such sharing. Skill in analyzing multiple policy and guidance documents then developing a logical, reasoned decisions regarding how those policies and guidance documents either authorize or denial of authorizing the sharing of information with international partners. Must demonstrate ability to communicate clearly, concisely, and accurately, using logic and evidence to convey the reasoning of a decision, both orally and in writing. Ability to work professionally with peers, management and international personnel is required; and ability to exercise a high level of tact and diplomacy. CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT CONTINUED: This position is covered by the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS), and as such will subject the incumbent to those examinations and/or tests that are necessary to obtain and retain a security clearance and any special accesses required by the position in accordance with AFI 36-1101. This position is a testing designated position and as such requires periodic urinalysis testing. Failure to comply with any of the special requirements, when required, will subject the incumbent of this position to reassignment or disciplinary adverse actions, including demotion or removal. Position is designated special-sensitive and requires eligibility for access to Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), other intelligence-related Special Sensitive information, or involvement in Top Secret Special Access Programs (SAP) to fully perform the duties and responsibilities of the position. A non-disclosure agreement must be signed. Drug Testing: This position has been designated by the Air Force as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Demand Reduction Program. Employee must pass initial and periodic short notice drug testing. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety. Ability to research legal issues, analyze complex factual situations in light of general legal principles and the results of research, and prepare legal opinions. 5. Ability to research legal issues, analyze complex factual situations in light of general legal principles and the results of research, and prepare legal opinions. 6. Ability to prepare cases for trial and/or try cases before a court, administrative body, or an official having quasi-judicial power.
